stemMd: In a test cross, an organism with genotype AaBb is crossed with aabb. The four offspring classes occur in roughly equal numbers. Which interpretation is most consistent with the data?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Every offspring is homozygous dominant at both loci.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The two loci assort independently or are sufficiently far apart to appear unlinked.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The AaBb parent can make only AB gametes.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Both loci must be on the same chromosome with no crossing over.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The data prove that meiosis never occurred.

explanationMd: The double-recessive tester makes only ab gametes, so each offspring phenotype reveals a gamete from AaBb. Four approximately equal classes correspond to AB, Ab, aB and ab gametes at similar frequencies. This supports independent assortment, but alone does not prove the loci lie on different chromosomes.

distractorRationale.c: Equal offspring classes require several gamete types.
distractorRationale.d: Complete linkage would not give four equal classes.
distractorRationale.a: The aabb parent supplies only recessive alleles.
distractorRationale.e: The pattern is consistent with ordinary meiosis and independent assortment.
